messages.subject: Error in quantile plot
parts:
Hello all,

I am trying to replicate a plot example (code below with attached image).  However when I run this code I get an Error:

"length(quantiles) == n is not TRUE"

data(Chem97, package = "mlmRev")

#GGplot#

p = ggplot(Chem97)
pg = p + geom_point(aes(sample = gcsescore), stat = "qq",  quantiles = ppoints(100)) + facet_wrap(~score)
print(pg)

Where is the error arising?  And how it is fixed?

Thanks,

 Art

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Error in quantile plot
parts:
Hi:

With a little reading between the lines on the help page, this appears to work:

p <- ggplot(Chem97, aes(sample = gcsescore))
p + stat_qq() + facet_wrap( ~ score) + ylab('gcsescore')

The problem with your code is that you tried to use ppoints(100), but
> table(Chem97$score)

   0    2    4    6    8   10
3688 3627 4619 5739 6668 6681

and that's why you got the error message - your attempt at defining y used a fixed number of ppoints() but there was inequality in the sample sizes in each score subgroup, all of which were not equal to 100. Using geom_point() with my above code doesn't work either because there is no 'y' defined. Since Hadley mentioned on the stat_qq() help page that qplot/ggplot was 'smart' enough to do the right thing, I trusted his word and voila :)

HTH,
Dennis
